Reported in one patient with dilated cardiomyopathy and endocardial fibroelastosis. It sits in a conserved region next to the first LIM domain and abolishes alpha-actinin-2 binding in cell culture. Segregation is not reported in the abstract.

The founding allele, c.10T>C in exon 2 according to the 2010 knock-in paper. It weakens telethonin binding and lowers MLP levels in knock-in mice. It is carried by up to 1% of people of European ancestry and did not segregate with dilated cardiomyopathy in the one family where segregation was tested. On current evidence it is best read as a common low-penetrance or benign variant, not a monogenic cause of this disease.

nodes.description: The proposed initiating lesion is a heterozygous germline missense variant in CSRP3. The reported dilated-cardiomyopathy alleles are W4R in the N-terminus and K69R, which lies in a conserved region next to the first LIM domain that is involved in alpha-actinin binding. W4R is a common European allele that did not segregate with disease in the one family where segregation was tested. Whether either allele causes dilated cardiomyopathy on its own is unresolved (see the discussions).

nodes.description: MLP anchors calcineurin at the Z-disc. When MLP is reduced, calcineurin is displaced and stress-induced calcineurin-NFAT activation is blunted. All evidence for this node is from mice and cultured cardiomyocytes.

nodes.description: MLP binds telethonin (T-cap), which in turn binds the N-terminus of titin, and alpha-actinin-2, the main Z-disc actin cross-linker. W4R weakens the telethonin interaction and K69R abolishes the alpha-actinin-2 interaction. In the founding study, telethonin was lost from the Z-disc in a subset of MLP-null mouse cardiomyocytes and in myocardial biopsies from W4R carriers. A dilated-cardiomyopathy variant in the partner, ACTN2 Q9R, also disrupts MLP binding, which supports the view that this complex is the relevant one.

nodes.description: Chronic inhibition of SERCA2a by phospholamban has been proposed as the calcium-cycling defect that drives chamber dilation in the MLP-null mouse, because ablating phospholamban rescues the phenotype. MLP-null hearts, however, are reported to have normal or enhanced SERCA function. The rescue may therefore work by bypassing the MLP lesion rather than by correcting it. MLP-null human stem-cell cardiomyocytes also show abnormal calcium handling, but they model hypertrophic rather than dilated disease. The node is HYPOTHETICAL for CMD1M.

evidence.reference_title: Chronic phospholamban-sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase interaction is the critical calcium cycling defect in dilated cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: The ablation of a muscle-specific sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA2a) inhibitor, phospholamban, rescued the spectrum of phenotypes that resemble human heart failure.

evidence.reference_title: MLP-deficient human pluripotent stem cell derived cardiomyocytes develop hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and heart failure phenotypes due to abnormal calcium handling.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, restoration of Ca2+ homeostasis by verapamil prevented the development of HCM and HF phenotypes, suggesting that elevated intracellular Ca2+ concentration is a central mechanism for pathogenesis of MLP deficiency.
